summary:
ASTRO COMMAND is an interactive 3D Solar System Exploration and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed to make space science engaging for students.

The platform allows users to explore planets, discover lunar and Martian environments, and understand the challenges of astronaut survival beyond Earth.

Its key features include a 3D Solar System, Moon Shackleton Crater Base, Mars Jezero Crater Base, Mission Control Dashboard, life-support monitoring, Planetary Survival Matrix, NASA science resources, STEM Learning Lab, and Astronaut Achievement System.

Through interactive visualizations and simulated environments, students learn about oxygen supply, water management, food production, solar energy, and radiation protection.

Our primary target audience is students aged 10–18, STEM educators, and space enthusiasts.

Our vision is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers through interactive space education.
details:
ASTRO COMMAND – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Astro Command is an interactive space exploration and astronaut training platform designed to help students understand the challenges of living and working beyond Earth. It provides an engaging virtual environment where users can explore the Solar System, discover the Moon and Mars, and learn about astronaut survival in space.

The platform includes interactive planetary exploration, lunar and Martian habitat concepts, a Mission Control dashboard, and a Planetary Survival Matrix. Users can learn about essential life-support resources such as oxygen, water, food, and energy while exploring concepts like radiation protection, hydroponics, and sustainable space habitats.

Our project aims to make complex space science concepts easier to understand through interactive learning and simulation. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, and interest in STEM education, especially among students.

We developed the project using web technologies and AI-assisted development tools. NASA-related scientific resources and publicly available space science information help support the educational experience.

Astro Command combines exploration, simulation, and education to give students an opportunity to experience the challenges of becoming an astronaut.
